es: Escribir un post con humor y lenguaje figurado ajustado al público, y adaptar una imagen que podría confundir a otro lector.

teaching.en: My post about the lost dog started with a hook: “I felt like a fish out of water.”
teaching.es: Mi publicación sobre el perro perdido empezó con un gancho: «Me sentía como pez fuera del agua».
teaching.explanationEs: El gancho es la primera línea: una imagen breve que despierta curiosidad.
segments: My post about the lost dog started with a
hook: “I felt like a fish out of water.”
teaching.audioText: My post about the lost dog started with a hook: “I felt like a fish out of water.”

teaching.en: Think about your audience: a friend gets the joke, but a stranger may not.
teaching.es: Piensa en tu público: un amigo entiende la broma, pero un desconocido quizá no.
teaching.explanationEs: Con amigos, humor y modismos; con desconocidos, imágenes universales.
segments: Think about your audience: a friend gets
the joke, but a stranger may not.
teaching.audioText: Think about your audience: a friend gets the joke, but a stranger may not.

teaching.en: My friend laughed, but the idiom was confusing for a reader from another country.
teaching.es: Mi amigo se rio, pero el modismo era confuso para un lector de otro país.
teaching.explanationEs: Un modismo muy local puede ser confuso: no es un error tuyo, pero sí un riesgo.
segments: My friend laughed, but the idiom was
confusing for a reader from another country.
teaching.audioText: My friend laughed, but the idiom was confusing for a reader from another country.

teaching.en: If an image is confusing, adapt it: say “I felt lost” instead of “I was a fish out of water”.
teaching.es: Si una imagen es confusa, adáptala: di «me sentía perdido» en lugar de «era un pez fuera del agua».
teaching.explanationEs: Adaptar = sustituir la imagen por un sentido directo.
segments: If an image is confusing, adapt it: say “I felt
lost” instead of “I was a fish out of water”.
teaching.audioText: If an image is confusing, adapt it: say “I felt lost” instead of “I was a fish out of water”.

teaching.en: I was not literally flying: I was over the moon after the good news.
teaching.es: No volaba al pie de la letra: estaba felicísimo tras la buena noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Literally se usa con el sentido real; over the moon es el sentido figurado.
segments: I was not literally flying: I was
over the moon after the good news.
teaching.audioText: I was not literally flying: I was over the moon after the good news.

teaching.en: The anecdote ends with a spark: one funny image, not five.
teaching.es: La anécdota termina con una chispa: una imagen divertida, no cinco.
teaching.explanationEs: La chispa es un toque de humor al final; con una basta.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es un buen gancho para un post?

choices.text: This post is about my day.
Yesterday I felt like a fish out of water at the gym.
I am writing to tell you something.

feedback.es: Un gancho despierta curiosidad con una imagen y un hecho; las otras frases no dicen nada concreto.

hint.es: Un gancho despierta curiosidad con una imagen y un dato.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si una imagen es confusa, adáptala.»

feedback.es: Confusing describe una imagen que el lector puede no entender; entonces se adapta.

hint.es: Significa «difícil de entender» y termina en -ing.

origin.text: If an image is ___, adapt it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Piensa en tu audiencia antes de elegir la imagen.»

answer.text: Think about your audience before you choose the image
accepted: Think about your audience before you choose the image
Before you choose the image think about your audience

feedback.es: El público decide qué imagen funciona, así que se piensa antes de escribir.

hint.es: Empieza con la orden y termina con lo que eliges.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su sentido.

feedback.es: Cada expresión tiene un sentido concreto que conviene aclarar si el lector es de otro país.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la persona cambió la frase.

choices.text: Because the text was too long.

feedback.es: La persona escribió «over the moon» para sus amigos y «very pleased» para su profesor: cambia según el público.

origin.audio: My post was for friends, so I wrote that I was over the moon. For my teacher I wrote that I was very pleased.

feedback.es: Over the moon va seguido de about + la causa de la alegría.

origin.text: I was over the moon ___ the news.

prompt.es: ¿Qué cambio aclara la imagen de Ana para lectores de otros países?

choices.text: I felt lost and out of place.
I felt like a fish in water.
I felt like a fish and a bird.

feedback.es: «Lost and out of place» dice el sentido directamente; «a fish in water» significa lo contrario y mezclar pez y pájaro añade otra imagen confusa.

origin.text: Ana is writing for readers in other countries. Her draft says: “I felt like a fish out of water.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué duda tiene la persona sobre su post.

choices.text: Whether a stranger will understand the image.
Whether the post is too short.

feedback.es: Pregunta si un desconocido entenderá la imagen: es la duda de adaptar el modismo a otro público.

origin.audio: Here's my post: I was over the moon after the good news. Do you think a stranger will understand it?

prompt.es: Completa: «No volaba al pie de la letra; solo estaba muy contento.»

feedback.es: Literally significa «al pie de la letra»: aclara que la imagen no era real.

origin.text: I was not ___ flying; I was just very happy.

prompt.es: Escribe un post con símil, metáfora, modismo y una versión directa (70–100 palabras).

answer.text: On Monday I ran like the wind to catch the bus, and I still missed it. The morning was a storm: rain, wind and a broken umbrella. Then a stranger shared his umbrella, and I was over the moon. I mean, I was really happy, because we walked together and he told me about his dog. His kindness saved my day, and now I always share my umbrella with other people. Have you ever had a day like that?
accepted: On Monday I ran like the wind to catch the bus, and I still missed it. The morning was a storm: rain, wind and a broken umbrella. Then a stranger shared his umbrella, and I was over the moon. I mean, I was really happy, because we walked together and he told me about his dog. His kindness saved my day, and now I always share my umbrella with other people. Have you ever had a day like that?

On Monday I ran like the wind to catch the bus, but I missed it. The morning was a storm: rain, wind and a broken umbrella. A stranger shared his umbrella, and I was over the moon. In other words, I was very happy, because his kindness was a spark on a grey day. Have you ever had a day like that?

I ran as fast as the wind to catch the bus on Monday, and I still missed it. The morning was a storm with rain and a broken umbrella. Then a stranger shared his umbrella, and I was over the moon. I mean, I felt very happy: his kindness was a spark on a grey day. Has that happened to you?

feedback.es: Un post con chispa cuenta una anécdota con datos reales, usa tres recursos figurados y aclara una imagen para el público de otros países.

origin.text: Anécdota: el lunes corriste para coger el autobús y lo perdiste; llovía y se rompió tu paraguas, pero un desconocido te ofreció el suyo. Escribe un post para seguidores de varios países: un símil, una metáfora, un modismo y una versión directa que aclare la imagen que podría confundir.

prompt.es: ¿Qué post es más seguro para lectores de otros países?

choices.text: Post A, because idioms are always clear.
Post B, because it says the meaning directly.

feedback.es: Post B dice el sentido directamente; un modismo como over the moon puede no entenderlo un lector extranjero.

origin.text: Post A: “I was over the moon.” Post B: “I was very happy.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál fue el gancho del post.

choices.text: An image of feeling out of place.
A list of exercises for the gym.

feedback.es: El gancho es la primera frase: una imagen de sentirse fuera de lugar en un gimnasio nuevo.

origin.audio: My post had a hook: I felt like a fish out of water at the new gym. Then I told the anecdote in order.

prompt.es: Adapta la imagen «fish out of water» para un lector que no la conozca.

answer.text: I felt nervous and strange at the gym.
accepted: I felt nervous and strange at the gym.
I felt very lost at the gym.
I was nervous at the new gym.

feedback.es: Adaptar es decir el sentido directamente: nervioso, perdido o extraño en el gimnasio.

origin.text: Adapta esta frase para alguien que no conoce el modismo: «I felt like a fish out of water at the gym.»
